title: Demonstration in Orléans against the National Rally party congress

tea.why: Protesters marched against the National Rally party congress and its politics, denouncing racism, fascism, and imperialism.
tea.want: Demonstrators chanted slogans against the National Rally and President Emmanuel Macron, demanding their removal.
tea.changed: Oct 24: Thousands marched in Orléans amid heavy security and a night curfew for minors.

summary: Thousands of people gathered in Orléans, France, on Saturday to participate in a demonstration against the National Rally party's national congress. The protest was called by around 50 political parties, trade unions, and associations, including figures such as Saint-Denis mayor Bally Bagayoko, Socialist Party leader Olivier Faure, and CGT union chief Sophie Binet. Participants marched through the city chanting slogans against far-right policies and President Emmanuel Macron, carrying banners opposing the far-right. Authorities deployed heavy security, including nearly 3,000 police officers, armored vehicles, water cannons, helicopters, and drones, while local officials implemented a nighttime curfew for individuals under 15 years old.
response: According to sources, authorities deployed nearly 3,000 police officers and gendarmes with armored vehicles, water cannons, helicopters, and drones. The local mayor instituted a nighttime curfew for individuals under 15 years of age during the weekend.

updates.text: Oct 24: Thousands of protesters marched in Orléans against the National Rally congress, according to reports.
